This draft illustrates the format available for short mathematical posts. Write

$$
e(\alpha)=e^{2\pi i\alpha}
$$

and consider the finite exponential sum

$$
S_N(\alpha)=\sum_{1\leq n\leq N} e(\alpha n).
$$ {#eq-geometric-sum}

If $\alpha\notin\mathbb Z$, the geometric-series identity gives

$$
S_N(\alpha)
=e(\alpha)\frac{1-e(\alpha N)}{1-e(\alpha)}.
$$

Consequently, @eq-geometric-sum satisfies

$$
|S_N(\alpha)|\leq \min\left\{N,\frac{1}{2\|\alpha\|}\right\},
$$

where $\|\alpha\|$ denotes the distance from $\alpha$ to the nearest integer. This elementary estimate already exhibits a basic feature of the circle method: an exponential sum can be large only when its frequency lies close to a rational point with small denominator.
